question: As of November 2026, which crewed mission holds the record for the farthest distance humans have traveled from Earth?
answer:
Artemis II broke the Apollo 13 record for the farthest distance travelled from Earth by a crewed mission, according to ESA [2]. On April 6, 2026, Orion and its crew flew past the Moon and broke the Apollo 13 record for the farthest distance travelled from Earth [2]. The crew were NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover and Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen [2]. The sources don't give the exact distance reached.

Voyager 1 is much farther from Earth, but it is an uncrewed probe, so it doesn't count for crewed missions [3][4].

keyPoints.text: Artemis II, a crewed flight, orbited the Moon and on April 6, 2026 broke the Apollo 13 record for the farthest distance traveled from Earth.
The Artemis II crew of four flew past the Moon on a free-return trajectory and returned safely, splashing down on April 11, 2026 local time.
NASA describes Artemis II as the first crewed flight aboard its human deep space capabilities, circling the Moon.
Voyager 1 is an uncrewed spacecraft and is not relevant to the crewed distance record.
